n: Moses looks far ahead, past the scattering. Even in exile among the nations, Israel will remember these words. Hope is built into the covenant.

f.w: thou shalt call them to mind
f.g: Literally “bring them back to your heart.”

n: The key is returning — repentance — with heart and soul, for both parents and children.

f.g: Hebrew shuv, “turn back,” the Old Testament word for repentance.

n: Then God will reverse their fortunes, show compassion, and gather them from every nation. This promise of gathering is central to the Restoration.

f.w: gather thee from all the nations

n: No one is too far away — even from the ends of the sky, God will bring his people home.

f.g: The farthest horizons — the ends of the earth.

n: They will possess the land again and be even more prosperous and numerous than their ancestors.
Here God himself changes their hearts. What Israel was told to do (10:16), God promises to do for them — a prophecy of the new covenant and the grace of Christ.
The curses will be turned against Israel’s enemies and persecutors.
Israel, with a new heart, will obey.
God will once more delight in blessing them with abundance in work, family, herds, and harvest.

f.w: the LORD will again rejoice over thee for good

n: The promise is tied to wholehearted turning and obedience to the written law.
God’s commandment is not mysterious or out of reach.

f.w: it is not hidden from thee
f.g: Not too hard or too wonderful for you.

n: No one needs to climb to heaven to fetch it — God has already brought it down.
No one must cross the sea to find it.
It is right here — in your mouth and heart. Paul applied this to the word of faith in Christ, who came near to us.

f.w: the word is very nigh unto thee

n: The great choice: life and good, or death and evil. Agency is God’s gift.

f.w: life and good, and death and evil

n: Choosing life means loving God, walking his ways, and keeping his commandments — which brings life, growth, and blessing in the land.

f.w: that thou mayest live and multiply

n: But turning the heart away, refusing to listen, and being lured to other gods…
…will lead to certain ruin and shortened life in the land.
Heaven and earth are called as witnesses. Then Moses pleads: “choose life” — for yourselves and your children. This is one of scripture’s great invitations.

f.w: I call heaven and earth to record

n: Life is not just a reward from God — God himself is their life. Loving him, obeying, and clinging to him is what living truly means.
